**Esegine Allen** (born 28 March 1986), better known by his stage name **Orezi**, is a Nigerian musician from Delta State. He rose to prominence with his song "Rihanna" in 2013.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-3)
In a chat with Showtime's _The Cooking Pot_ the singer said that in the Nigerian music industry, having talent without money is a waste of time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-4)

## Early life and education
[edit]
Esegine "Orezi" Allen was born and raised in Owhelogbo, Isoko, Delta State. He is the first born of five children. Orezi attended the Command Secondary School in Abakaliki. He graduated from the University of Lagos and completed the mandatory one-year NYSC program.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-5)
Orezi began his music career in early 2009. He has worked with several producers, including Kiddominant, Del B and Dokta Frabz.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-7) Orezi's debut song "I No Fit Lie" became Radio Continental's theme song. He headlined a show named after the song; the show was organised by the Continental Broadcasting Services (CBS).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-8) The music video for "I No Fit Lie" was shot in South Africa. In 2010, Orezi released the single "High B.P". The music video for the song was endorsed by MTV Base.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-9) In late 2010, he released the DJ JamJam-assisted track "Jamilaya".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-10)

## Early life and education
In early 2011, Orezi was featured on "Emoti" alongside Danagog, Igho and DJ Debby. The song was played on Trace TV, MTV Base, Soundcity and One Music. He was also featured on Jatt's single "Komije" alongside Sauce Kid, Muna and Igho. Orezi released the music video for the song "Booty Bounce"; it features cameo appearances from Karen Igho, Bovi, Wande Coal, Kay Switch, Sina Rambo, Vina, Danagog, Skuki and General Pype, among others. For several weeks, "Booty Bounce" was one of the top ten African songs on Trace Urban, Channel O and MTV. The music video for "Booty Bounce" was nominated for Most Gifted Reggae Video of the Year at the 2012 Channel O Music Video Awards.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-11)
In 2010, Orezi performed during Star Music Trek's visit to Kaduna and Makurdi, and also performed at an event celebrating Nigeria's 50th Independence Day. In early 2011, Orezi performed at DJ Jimmy Jatt's "Jump Off" show held at the Get Arena in Lekki. He has performed in several club tours in Nigeria and South Africa. He was part of the Emoti Tour organized by DJ Debby. Orezi performed at Club Inc in South Africa. In 2012, he performed at the Rhythm Unplugged concert in Ibadan, and toured with Trace Urban and St. Remy.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-12)

## Early life and education
Orezi released the single "You Garrit" in November 2013; the song's music video was released in September 2014.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-13) On 27 March 2014, Orezi released "Shoki" as the fourth single off his debut studio album _The Gehn Gehn Album_ (2015). Orezi said the inspiration for "Shoki" came after he returned from South Africa, went to the Afrika Shrine, and saw people doing the Shoki dance. He asked about the dance, learned its name, and later, while in the studio with producer Popito (who had sent him a beat), he created the song around it. Orezi admitted he did not know the meaning of “Shoki”, only that it was the name of the dance. He clarified that he did not invent the dance, which he said originated from Agege or somewhere else, and that it already existed before his song. Orezi said his and Lil Kesh’s versions of “Shoki” were released around the same time, with Lil Kesh’s version appearing online slightly earlier. He acknowledged that many other artists recorded “Shoki” songs (more than three versions existed), but suggested that his gained more attention because he was already a recognized artist.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-14) In March 2014, Orezi released the French version of his single "Shoki".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-15) On 15 December 2014, Orezi released a four-track EP for the different versions of "Shoki".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-16) Orezi released his debut album _The Ghen Ghen Album_ in September 2015. It features collaborations with 9ice, Davido, [Flavour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavour_N'abania "Flavour N'abania"), Ice Prince, M.I Abaga, Timaya and Wizkid.

## Early life and education
Pulse Nigeria awarded the album 3 stars out of 5.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-17) In November 2015, Orezi released the music video for his single "Ogede" featuring Wizkid and Timaya. The music video was directed by Paul Gambit.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-18) In September 2016, he released the controversial single "Call the Police".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-19)

**Esegine Allen** (born 28 March 1986), better known by his stage name **Orezi**, is a Nigerian musician from Delta State. He rose to prominence with his song "Rihanna" in 2013.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-3)
In a chat with Showtime's _The Cooking Pot_ the singer said that in the Nigerian music industry, having talent without money is a waste of time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-4)
texts.1:
## Early life and education
[edit]
Esegine "Orezi" Allen was born and raised in Owhelogbo, Isoko, Delta State. He is the first born of five children. Orezi attended the Command Secondary School in Abakaliki. He graduated from the University of Lagos and completed the mandatory one-year NYSC program.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-5)
Orezi began his music career in early 2009. He has worked with several producers, including Kiddominant, Del B and Dokta Frabz.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-7) Orezi's debut song "I No Fit Lie" became Radio Continental's theme song. He headlined a show named after the song; the show was organised by the Continental Broadcasting Services (CBS).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-8) The music video for "I No Fit Lie" was shot in South Africa. In 2010, Orezi released the single "High B.P". The music video for the song was endorsed by MTV Base.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-9) In late 2010, he released the DJ JamJam-assisted track "Jamilaya".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-10)
texts.2:
## Early life and education
In early 2011, Orezi was featured on "Emoti" alongside Danagog, Igho and DJ Debby. The song was played on Trace TV, MTV Base, Soundcity and One Music. He was also featured on Jatt's single "Komije" alongside Sauce Kid, Muna and Igho. Orezi released the music video for the song "Booty Bounce"; it features cameo appearances from Karen Igho, Bovi, Wande Coal, Kay Switch, Sina Rambo, Vina, Danagog, Skuki and General Pype, among others. For several weeks, "Booty Bounce" was one of the top ten African songs on Trace Urban, Channel O and MTV. The music video for "Booty Bounce" was nominated for Most Gifted Reggae Video of the Year at the 2012 Channel O Music Video Awards.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-11)
In 2010, Orezi performed during Star Music Trek's visit to Kaduna and Makurdi, and also performed at an event celebrating Nigeria's 50th Independence Day. In early 2011, Orezi performed at DJ Jimmy Jatt's "Jump Off" show held at the Get Arena in Lekki. He has performed in several club tours in Nigeria and South Africa. He was part of the Emoti Tour organized by DJ Debby. Orezi performed at Club Inc in South Africa. In 2012, he performed at the Rhythm Unplugged concert in Ibadan, and toured with Trace Urban and St. Remy.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-12)
texts.3:
## Early life and education
Orezi released the single "You Garrit" in November 2013; the song's music video was released in September 2014.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-13) On 27 March 2014, Orezi released "Shoki" as the fourth single off his debut studio album _The Gehn Gehn Album_ (2015). Orezi said the inspiration for "Shoki" came after he returned from South Africa, went to the Afrika Shrine, and saw people doing the Shoki dance. He asked about the dance, learned its name, and later, while in the studio with producer Popito (who had sent him a beat), he created the song around it. Orezi admitted he did not know the meaning of “Shoki”, only that it was the name of the dance. He clarified that he did not invent the dance, which he said originated from Agege or somewhere else, and that it already existed before his song. Orezi said his and Lil Kesh’s versions of “Shoki” were released around the same time, with Lil Kesh’s version appearing online slightly earlier. He acknowledged that many other artists recorded “Shoki” songs (more than three versions existed), but suggested that his gained more attention because he was already a recognized artist.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-14) In March 2014, Orezi released the French version of his single "Shoki".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-15) On 15 December 2014, Orezi released a four-track EP for the different versions of "Shoki".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orezi#cite_note-16) Orezi released his debut album _The Ghen Ghen Album_ in September 2015. It features collaborations with 9ice, Davido, [Flavour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavour_N'abania "Flavour N'abania"), Ice Prince, M.I Abaga, Timaya and Wizkid.

#### Hon. Justice Theresa Obiajulu Ogochukwu Diai
Hon. Chief Judge of Delta State
Hon. Justice Theresa T. Obiajulu Ogochukwu Diai was appointed as the Acting Chief Judge of Delta State on May 24, 2021, following the retirement of Hon. Justice Marshal Umukoro. Her appointment was confirmed after the recommendation by the National Judicial Council, in accordance with Section 271(1) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended).
Justice Diai's legal career is marked by dedication and a commitment to justice. She has served in various capacities within the judiciary, including as Chairman of the Judicial Panel of Inquiry on the Okpe-Usobo Forest Reserve. Her leadership has been instrumental in enhancing access to justice in Delta State, with the creation of new judicial divisions and magisterial districts under her tenure.
As Chief Judge, she has emphasized the importance of integrity, accountability, and discipline within the judiciary. She continues to advocate for judicial reforms and the welfare of judicial officers in the state.
Justice Diai is also a member of the Welfare Events and Benchers Programmes Committee of the Body of Benchers, contributing to the development of the legal profession at the national level.
Her appointment as the Chief Judge of Delta State marks a significant milestone, as she is among the few women to have held this esteemed position, reflecting the progress in gender representation within the Nigerian judiciary.

Chunks: 0
Following the enactment of the Administration of Criminal Justice Law 2022 and the Administration of Civil Justice Law 2022 in Delta State the Delta State Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice Isaiah Bozimo, Esq
convened a workshop for a broad range of actors and stakeholders. The workshop which held from the 10th to the 12th of May 2023, centred around the innovations and fundamental aspects of the two laws which are already being acknowledged as trailblazers in the country’s legal framework.
The workshop was attended by the Chief Judge and the Honourable Judges of the High Court of Delta State and the first and second days of the workshop x-rayed the Administration of civil Justice Law and the Administration of Criminal Justice Law respectively.
The sessions for the first day examined Pre-litigation Requirements and Costs, Active Case Management. Alternative Dispute Resolution and Interim Remedies Reference (IRR) and the role of Information Technology within the justice system. The sessions were facilitated by senior lawyers which included Mrs Funke Adekoya SAN and Babatunde Fagbohunlu SAN
Similarly, the criminal justice sessions were helmed by an array of industry stalwarts. Prof. Yemi Akinseye George, SAN, provided a comprehensive overview of the new provisions within the Administration of Criminal Justice Law, 2022. Chino Obiagwu, SAN, dissected the Case Management provisions, while Prof. Festus Emiri, SAN, elucidated on the Sentencing and Restitution provisions.
The concluding day broadened the scope of participation to include a diverse range of stakeholders. This included Magistrates, Presidents of Area Customary Courts, Court Registrars, State Counsel from the Ministry of Justice, Legal Aid Council, representatives from the Department of State Services, Nigeria Correctional Service and officers from the Nigerian Police Force.
In his closing remarks the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Delta State, Isaiah Bozimo, Esq.underscored the commitment of the Ministry of Justice to continuous capacity building for staff. True to his words he unveiled detailed implementation workbooks for the Civil and Criminal Justice Laws of Delta State which are designed to guide application of the laws and the adoption of best legal practices in their implementation.

Dispense Justice Without Fear Or Favour, Oborevwori Tells Judges
Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, has charged judges in the state to dispense justice without fear or favour, assuring them of his administration’s commitment to judicial independence, improved welfare and efficient justice delivery.
Oborevwori gave the charge on Tuesday when he received judges of the state judiciary, led by the Chief Judge, Justice Theresa Diai, at Government House, Asaba, as part of activities marking the 2026/2027 legal year.
He urged the judges to remain impartial, stressing that; "nobody is above the law, and we will not allow anybody to take the law into his or her hands. I encourage you to do your work without fear or favour. Do the right thing; it is not about the government or any individual,” he said.
The governor urged the judges to handle cases involving kidnapping, armed robbery and murder with the seriousness they deserved, noting that effective justice delivery was critical to sustaining peace and security in the state.
On judicial welfare, Oborevwori said his administration was constructing five judges’ quarters in Warri and another five in Asaba, assuring that the projects would be completed by the end of the first quarter of 2027.

He also pledged continued support for the training of judges and the provision of modern court equipment, including stenographic machines for the verbatim recording of court proceedings.
The governor further approved requests for improved security and additional solar power installations in courts across the state to protect judicial facilities and ensure the effective operation of digital court equipment.
Earlier, Justice Diai commended the governor for improvements in judicial training, information and communications technology, and court infrastructure, including the renovation of High Courts, magistrate courts and customary courts.
She disclosed that 20 judges had been sponsored for overseas training, while equipment for electronic filing and virtual hearings had been deployed to the High Courts.
However, the Chief Judge appealed for adequate security at court facilities and additional solar power installations in judicial divisions where existing units were insufficient.
Justice Diai expressed appreciation for the administration’s support and called for sustained collaboration to strengthen the judiciary and improve justice delivery in Delta State.

#### Hon. Justice Theresa Obiajulu Ogochukwu Diai
Hon. Chief Judge of Delta State
Hon. Justice Theresa T. Obiajulu Ogochukwu Diai was appointed as the Acting Chief Judge of Delta State on May 24, 2021, following the retirement of Hon. Justice Marshal Umukoro. Her appointment was confirmed after the recommendation by the National Judicial Council, in accordance with Section 271(1) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended).
Justice Diai's legal career is marked by dedication and a commitment to justice. She has served in various capacities within the judiciary, including as Chairman of the Judicial Panel of Inquiry on the Okpe-Usobo Forest Reserve. Her leadership has been instrumental in enhancing access to justice in Delta State, with the creation of new judicial divisions and magisterial districts under her tenure.
As Chief Judge, she has emphasized the importance of integrity, accountability, and discipline within the judiciary. She continues to advocate for judicial reforms and the welfare of judicial officers in the state.
Justice Diai is also a member of the Welfare Events and Benchers Programmes Committee of the Body of Benchers, contributing to the development of the legal profession at the national level.
Her appointment as the Chief Judge of Delta State marks a significant milestone, as she is among the few women to have held this esteemed position, reflecting the progress in gender representation within the Nigerian judiciary.

Dispense Justice Without Fear Or Favour, Oborevwori Tells Judges
Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, has charged judges in the state to dispense justice without fear or favour, assuring them of his administration’s commitment to judicial independence, improved welfare and efficient justice delivery.
Oborevwori gave the charge on Tuesday when he received judges of the state judiciary, led by the Chief Judge, Justice Theresa Diai, at Government House, Asaba, as part of activities marking the 2026/2027 legal year.
He urged the judges to remain impartial, stressing that; "nobody is above the law, and we will not allow anybody to take the law into his or her hands. I encourage you to do your work without fear or favour. Do the right thing; it is not about the government or any individual,” he said.
The governor urged the judges to handle cases involving kidnapping, armed robbery and murder with the seriousness they deserved, noting that effective justice delivery was critical to sustaining peace and security in the state.
On judicial welfare, Oborevwori said his administration was constructing five judges’ quarters in Warri and another five in Asaba, assuring that the projects would be completed by the end of the first quarter of 2027.
